title: Caprese sandwiches
skill: Slicing soft foods with a paring knife

notes.text: Slice everything first, then build the sandwiches in a row, like an assembly line.

move.title: A small knife, soft foods
move.body: Today you'll use a paring knife on two soft foods, tomato and fresh mozzarella, and a bread knife on the rolls. Layered with basil and olive oil, they make an Italian sandwich with no cooking at all.

why.title: A board that can't slide
why.body: Most knife cuts happen when the board or the food moves. A damp paper towel under the board holds it still, and a flat side down holds the food still.

why.title: The bridge grip
why.body: To cut something round in half, make a bridge over it with your hand: thumb on one side, fingers on the other. The knife goes under the bridge, so your fingers are never in its path.

why.title: The claw grip
why.body: To slice, curl your fingertips under and rest your knuckles against the side of the blade. The blade can only touch your knuckles, and it slides along them instead of cutting.

why.title: Saw, don't press
why.body: Tomato skin is tough and the inside is soft. Pressing straight down squashes it. Small back-and-forth strokes let the edge cut through the skin first.

why.title: Where the knife goes
why.body: When you're not cutting, the knife lies flat at the top of the board, blade facing away from you. Never leave it near the edge, under food, or in a sink of soapy water, where someone can't see it.

wrong.sign: The tomato squashed instead of slicing
wrong.fix: Use small sawing strokes and let the knife do the work. If it still squashes, the knife may be dull; ask an adult to hone it.
Wet the paper towel again and press the board down onto it.
Pat the tomato and mozzarella slices dry with a paper towel before they go on the bread.

wrong.sign: The slices are thick and thin
wrong.fix: Slow down. Move your claw hand back the same small step after each cut.

quiz.q: What goes under the cutting board so it can't slide?
quiz.explain: A board that moves is how most cuts happen.

quiz.q: In the claw grip, what touches the side of the blade?
quiz.explain: Fingertips stay curled under, out of the way.

quiz.q: Where does the knife go when you're not cutting?
choices: Flat at the top of the board, blade away from you
On the edge of the counter

quiz.q: How do you slice a tomato without squashing it?
quiz.explain: The edge cuts the skin first.

substitutions.note: Use two slices of gluten-free bread for each sandwich, toasted so they hold up to the tomato.

steps.text: Wet a paper towel, squeeze it out, and lay it flat under the cutting board.
steps.look: Push the board gently. It shouldn't slide.

steps.text: Rinse the tomatoes and basil, and pat them dry with paper towels.
steps.tip: Dry food doesn't slip under the knife.

steps.text: Lay a tomato on the board. Hold it with the bridge grip and cut it in half from top to bottom with the paring knife.
steps.tip: The knife goes under your hand's bridge, never toward your fingers.

steps.text: Lay each half flat side down. Hold it with the claw grip and cut slices about ¼ inch thick.
steps.look: Slices about as thick as a pencil.

steps.text: Slice the second tomato the same way. Put the slices on the plate.
steps.tip: Use small sawing strokes, and let the knife do the work.

steps.text: Set the knife down flat at the top of the board, blade facing away from you.
steps.tip: Do this every time you stop cutting, even for a moment.

steps.text: Drain the mozzarella and pat it dry. Hold it with the claw grip and slice it about ¼ inch thick.
steps.look: Round slices about the same size as the tomato slices.

steps.text: Lay a roll flat. Press your hand flat on top and cut it open sideways with the bread knife, sawing gently.
steps.tip: Keep your fingers flat and pointing up, above the blade's path.

steps.text: Spoon a little olive oil over the cut sides of each roll.
steps.look: A light shine on the bread, not a puddle.

steps.text: On each bottom half, layer tomato slices, mozzarella slices, and basil leaves. Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
steps.tip: Overlap the slices a little so every bite has some of each.

steps.text: Put on the tops and press each sandwich down gently with your hand.
Wash the knives one at a time, holding the handle, with the blade pointing away from you. Dry them and put them away.
steps.tip: Never drop a knife into a sink of soapy water.
